report.releaseDate: 23 Oct 2026 (GCU casino revenue files "as of 20 Oct 2026"; sports wagering files week-ending 30 Sep 2026)
report.verdict: Maine is a small, two-casino, tribal-exclusive-mobile market growing low-single-digits: 9M 2026 land-based GGR was $129.4m (+2.3%), carried entirely by slots (+4.5%) while tables fell 10%, and sports handle rose 10% to $450.2m with September hold normalising to 10.4%. The state keeps ~42% of casino GGR and 10% of sports AGR, and the only route to the online casino upside is through the Wabanaki Nations — whose iGaming bill (LD 1164) remains the single swing factor for the next 12-24 months.
summary: **Headline: land-based GGR +2.3% to $129.4m in 9M 2026.** Gambling Control Unit (GCU) files for Hollywood Casino Bangor and Oxford Casino sum to $129,397,375 vs $126,445,679 in 9M 2025 — reconciling exactly to the Gaming Intelligence lead. Q3 accelerated to +4.8% ($47.0m) after a flat H1 (+1.0%, $82.4m); September was +7.5% ($15.4m).

**Product mix: slots carry the market, tables shrink.** Slot GGR $112.4m (+4.5%) was 86.9% of casino GGR; table GGR $17.0m (-10.1%). Oxford tables fell 18.3% (drop -8.1%, hold 20.8% vs 23.4%); Hollywood tables +0.7% on drop +12.2% but hold compressed to 21.9% from 24.4%.

**Operator split: Oxford (Churchill Downs) 59.2% / Hollywood (PENN) 40.8%.** Oxford 9M GGR $76.6m (flat, -0.03%); Hollywood $52.8m (+6.0%), the growth engine on slot volume (funds-in +15.4%) with 621 machines vs Oxford's ~946.

**Market size incl. sports: ~$178m in 9M 2026 (estimate).** Casino $129.4m (primary) plus sports AGR of ~$48.6m (derived from reported 9M tax of 'nearly $4.9m'; secondary). FY2025 was $234.6m per AGA: casino $166.4m (71%) + sports $68.2m (29%), the GCU casino figure matching AGA to within $0.1m.

**Online penetration ~27% — and it is sports-only.** Maine has no legal iGaming; mobile sports wagering (>99% of sports AGR per AGA) is the whole regulated online channel. Treat 'online share' as ~27% of total 9M GGR (estimate).

**Sports wagering 9M 2026: handle $450.2m (+10%), September AGR $6.34m (+36.5%).** September handle slipped 3.4% to $61.05m but hold rose to 10.4% from ~7.4%; DraftKings took $50.8m (83% share) at 10.7% hold. Four reporting groups file with the GCU: two mobile (DraftKings via Penobscot/Maliseet/Mi'kmaq; Caesars via Passamaquoddy) and two retail (Oxford Sportsbook; First Tracks Investments/Oddfellahs).

**Regulator and law.** The GCU sits within the Department of Public Safety, under a Gambling Control Board; casinos operate under Title 8 MRSA ch. 31 (slots/table games), sports wagering under ch. 35 (live since Nov 2023). Figures are 'subject to audit'. Lottery is run separately by BABLO and is excluded here (n/a).

**Casino tax base is GGR, and it is heavy: ~42% effective.** Hollywood: 1% of gross slot machine income (coin-in) + 39% of net slot income + 16% of net table income (effective 41.6% of GGR in 9M). Oxford: 46% of net slot income + 16% of net table income (effective 42.5%). 9M 2026 take $54.5m (+3.6%), Q3 $19.9m (+6.4%); FY2025 $69.3m.

**Sports tax is light: 10% of adjusted gross sports wagering receipts (AGR).** GCU page verified: 1% GCU admin, 1% Gambling Addiction Prevention & Treatment Fund, 0.55% harness racing, 0.55% Sire Stakes, 0.4% Agricultural Fair Promotion, 6.5% General Fund. September take $634k; 9M ~$4.9m. Plus 0.25% federal excise on handle.

**Combined state take 9M 2026 ≈ $59.4m** (casino $54.5m primary + sports ~$4.9m secondary). AGA puts FY2025 total gaming tax at $75.9m (+4.3%); GCU casino $69.3m + 10% of $68.2m sports = $76.2m, a $0.3m gap likely from base definitions.

**Licensing is closed in practice.** Two casino licences exist; statutory caps (3,000 slots statewide / 1,500 per facility; 100-mile siting restriction [not re-verified today]) and the referendum history mean a third property needs legislation. Mobile sports licences are reserved to the four Wabanaki Nations (one each; two skins live); retail facility licences are open to casinos, commercial tracks and OTBs. Mobile licence fee $200,000 per 4-year term [per Title 8 §1205; not re-verified today].

**Operator landscape: DraftKings dominates sports (~83% of September handle); Caesars is the distant #2.** PENN has no retail or ESPN Bet presence in Maine because mobile is tribal-exclusive; Oxford launched a retail book in 2025. The Portland Oddfellas retail book was denied a permanent licence in Jan 2025 (AGA), yet First Tracks Investments (Oddfellahs) still files 2026 revenue with the GCU — status detail [unverified].

**Payments reality is US-standard, not mobile-money.** ACH/online banking, debit and wallet rails via the DraftKings/Caesars platforms; the sports framework restricts credit-card funding of accounts [not re-verified today]. Casinos are cash/TITO-based with ~$1.1bn of 9M funds-in across the two floors.

**Responsible gambling and advertising are among the stricter US regimes.** Minimum age 21 for casino and sports; a GCU-administered statewide self-exclusion list; a dedicated Gambling Addiction Prevention and Treatment Fund funded from both verticals; Chapter 41 sports rules restrict college-campus advertising, under-21 imagery and 'risk-free' promotional language [rule detail not re-verified today].

**Direction of travel: tribal iGaming is the swing factor.** LD 1164 (Wabanaki-exclusive internet gaming) passed both chambers in 2025 but faced gubernatorial opposition and was carried over; its 2026 outcome could not be verified in this research [unverified]. Governor Mills is term-limited and Maine votes on 3 Nov 2026 — the next administration decides whether online casino arrives and who controls it.

**Hold normalisation is the near-term earnings lever in sports.** 9M hold ~10.8% (AGR ~$48.6m / handle $450.2m, estimate) vs AGA-implied 2025 levels; Q4 NFL volume will set FY2026 sports AGR, which we estimate at $70-75m (+3-10%).

**Read-through for B2Tech: a B2B/partner market, not a licence market.** There is no direct route to a mobile licence (tribal exclusivity), the two casinos are vertically owned by PENN and Churchill Downs, and retail sports is sub-1% of AGR. Realistic entries are (i) platform/content supply to the tribes' current or future partners, (ii) positioning for a tribal iGaming skin if LD 1164 or a successor passes, or (iii) ETG/cabinet supply to Oxford, which began reporting electronic table game win in June 2026.

segments.name: Land-based casinos (slots & table games)
segments.headline: Slots +4.5% carry a +2.3% market; tables -10% with hold compression at both properties; Hollywood outgrows Oxford.
narrative: The GCU's weekly-updated revenue distribution files put 9M 2026 net slot income at $112.44m (+4.5%) and net table income at $16.96m (-10.1%), for total GGR of $129.40m (+2.3%). The quarterly shape matters: H1 was essentially flat (+1.0% to $82.4m, with January -3.4% and May -0.6% offsetting February's +9.1%), and Q3 did all the work (+4.8% to $47.0m; July +3.5%, August +3.6%, September +7.5%). The first 20 days of October added a further $9.2m. All figures are gross of tax and before promotional allowances, which Maine does not net from the tax base.

Hollywood Casino Bangor (PENN Entertainment) generated $52.83m (+6.0%): slots $44.68m (+7.0%) on funds-in of $393m (+15.4%) across 621 machines (up from ~611 in 2025), implying slot hold on funds-in eased to 11.4% from 12.3% while GCU-reported win on coin-in was 8.43% (payback 91.57%). Its tables did $8.15m (+0.7%) on drop of $37.2m (+12.2%); hold fell to 21.9% from 24.4%, so volume growth was almost entirely given back in hold. Hollywood's implied coin-in from the 1% gross-slot-income line is ~$528m for 9M. Win per unit per day was ~$264 for slots and ~$2,300 per table (13 tables).

Oxford Casino (Churchill Downs) was flat at $76.57m (-0.03%): slots $67.76m (+3.0%) on funds-in of $706m (+8.4%) across ~946 machines (down from 959), win on coin-in 7.50% (payback 92.50%); tables $8.81m (-18.3%) on drop of $42.3m (-8.1%) with hold at 20.8% vs 23.4%. Slot win per unit per day was ~$262 — identical to Bangor despite a looser floor — while table win per table per day was ~$1,470 across 22 tables. Oxford began reporting an 'ETG win/loss' line in June 2026 ($0.20m through September; $0.25m through 20 Oct), the first new product line on the floor in years and a sign the operator is responding to table weakness with electronic table games.

Oxford's share of casino GGR slipped to 59.2% from 60.6% in 9M 2025. Both properties remain far below the statutory 1,500-machine per-facility cap (and the 3,000 statewide cap) [caps per Title 8 §1020; not re-verified today], so supply is not the constraint; the southern-Maine/New Hampshire border catchment and New England competition (Massachusetts' Encore and MGM Springfield, New Hampshire's charitable casinos and historical horse racing venues) set the ceiling. Full-year 2025 GGR was $166.36m (Hollywood $66.10m, Oxford $100.27m), reconciling with AGA's $141.9m EGD + $24.5m tables.

For an operator, the land-based segment is closed: two licences, both vertically owned by listed US groups, with no licensing window and a 100-mile siting rule [not re-verified today] that effectively requires legislation for a third property (tribal casino bills have surfaced repeatedly). Commercial relevance is as a supplier — cabinets, ETGs, systems — into a ~1,570-machine, 35-table estate where the state takes ~42% of GGR, which caps operator appetite for aggressive capex and promotions.

segments.name: Sports wagering (tribal mobile + retail)
segments.headline: Handle +10% to $450.2m in 9M; September AGR +36.5% on hold normalising to 10.4%; DraftKings ~83% share; retail immaterial.
narrative: Maine's sports wagering market (Title 8 ch. 35; live since 3 Nov 2023) reports through four GCU files: Penobscot Nation/Houlton Band of Maliseet/Mi'kmaq Nation (DraftKings), Passamaquoddy Tribe (Caesars Sportsbook), Oxford Sportsbook (retail, first full year 2026) and First Tracks Investments LLC (Oddfellahs retail). Three independent trade reads of the September files agree: 9M 2026 handle $450.2m (+10% YoY, implying ~$409m in 9M 2025), September handle $61.05m (-3.4% YoY, +23.8% MoM with the NFL), September AGR $6.34m (+36.5% YoY, +62.1% MoM) and September tax $634,222. The primary GCU PDFs could not be parsed within this research, so sports figures are tagged secondary; the Covers tracker's 9M figures ($444.5m handle / $48.6m AGR / 11.0% hold) differ marginally on handle — the GCU-sourced $450.2m is used.

Hold is the story. September 2026 hold of 10.4% compares with ~7.4% in September 2025 (AGA/trade), and DraftKings' own hold rose to 10.7% from 7.2%, lifting its AGR 42% to $5.4m on a 3.4% smaller handle of $50.8m. DraftKings' ~83% share of handle leaves Caesars at roughly 16% and the two retail books at well under 1% combined — AGA states the two mobile platforms accounted for more than 99% of 2025 sports revenue ($68.2m, +20.1%). Using the reported 9M tax of 'nearly $4.9m' at a 10% rate gives 9M AGR of ~$48.6m and a 9M hold of ~10.8% (estimate).

The economics for the licensees are attractive relative to the casinos: 10% of AGR with no promotional deduction [deduction treatment not re-verified today] plus the 0.25% federal excise on handle, versus ~42% of GGR for slots and tables. That asymmetry, plus the tribal exclusivity on mobile, explains why the casinos have lobbied for their own mobile access and why the tribes are now pressing to extend exclusivity into iGaming.

Retail is structurally marginal: Oxford opened its book in 2025; Hollywood Bangor has no reporting sportsbook (PENN's ESPN Bet has no Maine route); the Portland Oddfellas venue had its permanent licence application denied by the Gambling Control Board in January 2025, briefly pausing retail betting (AGA), although First Tracks Investments (Oddfellahs) continues to file 2026 revenue with the GCU — the current licensing basis is [unverified]. Facility licences remain available to commercial tracks and OTBs, but with handle under 1% of the state total there is no commercial case for a standalone retail entry.

Seasonality and the Q4 NFL/NBA run-in will set FY2026: if Q4 handle grows mid-single digits on the 2025 base and hold holds near 10%, FY2026 AGR lands around $70-75m (estimate, +3-10%). For an operator, the only mobile entry is as a tribe's platform partner; two of the four nations' skins are contracted to DraftKings and one to Caesars, with the Mi'kmaq/Maliseet rights bundled into the DraftKings arrangement — meaning no uncontracted skin exists today.

segments.name: Licensing, tax & revenue distribution
segments.headline: Closed casino duopoly taxed at ~42% of GGR; tribal-exclusive mobile taxed at 10% of AGR; statutory earmarks route proceeds to education, racing and agriculture.
narrative: The Gambling Control Unit (Department of Public Safety) licenses and audits casinos, sports wagering, fantasy contests, harness racing/OTB and charitable gaming; a five-member Gambling Control Board adjudicates licences. Casinos operate under Title 8 MRSA ch. 31 as enacted by referendum (Bangor 2003; Oxford 2010), with table games added in 2012. Supply is capped by statute at 3,000 slot machines statewide and 1,500 per facility, and new facilities face a 100-mile siting restriction [caps and siting rule not re-verified today], so in practice the only path to a third venue is a legislative act — bills for a Wabanaki casino have been filed in successive sessions without passage.

Casino taxation is on GGR and is among the heaviest in the US. For Hollywood Bangor, Title 8 §1036 requires 1% of gross slot machine income (coin-in; $5.28m in 9M 2026 implying ~$528m coin-in) to the General Fund, plus 39% of net slot machine income distributed to twelve earmarks (10% Fund for a Healthy Maine, 10% harness racing purses, 4% Fund to Encourage Racing at commercial tracks, 3% GCU administration/gambling addiction, 3% Agricultural Fair Support, 3% Sire Stakes, 2% University of Maine scholarships, 1% each to Maine Community College System, OTB stabilisation and host municipality Bangor, with a Maine Maritime Academy slice). Oxford pays 46% of net slot income (25% Department of Education K-12, 4% UMaine scholarships, 4% Penobscot and Passamaquoddy Tribes, 3% MCCS, 3% GCU, 2% Town of Oxford, 1% each to agricultural fairs, harness purses, Sire Stakes and Oxford County, 0.5% each to dairy improvement and the milk pool). Both pay 16% of net table game income (Bangor: 9% General Fund, 3% GCU special revenue, 2% Veterans Assistance, 2% Bangor; Oxford: 10% K-12, 3% GCU, 2% town, 1% county).

The resulting 9M 2026 state take was $54.53m (+3.6%): Hollywood $21.95m (41.6% of its GGR), Oxford $32.58m (42.5%). FY2025 take was $69.34m on $166.36m GGR (41.7%). Because the Hollywood 1% line is levied on coin-in, its effective burden rises when hold falls — a small but real volatility an operator should model.

Sports wagering is taxed at 10% of adjusted gross sports wagering receipts (gross receipts less winnings paid and federal excise), distributed per the GCU: 1% to GCU administration, 1% to the Gambling Addiction Prevention and Treatment Fund, 0.55% to the Harness Racing Commission, 0.55% to the Sire Stakes Fund, 0.4% to the Agricultural Fair Promotion Fund and 6.5% to the General Fund. Mobile sports wagering licences are reserved to the four federally recognised Wabanaki Nations (one each; $200,000 per four-year term [Title 8 §1205; not re-verified today]); facility licences are open to the casinos, commercial tracks and OTBs; suppliers and management-services providers need their own licences. Proposals to raise the sports rate (a 16% figure was floated in 2025 budget deliberations) did not appear on the GCU's current page, which still states 10% [legislative outcome unverified].

The commercial reading: Maine's fiscal design deliberately favours the tribes (10% on mobile sports) and the state's earmarked beneficiaries (42% on casinos). Any iGaming statute will be negotiated inside this frame — expect a tribal-exclusive model with a rate pitched between the two (the 2025 LD 1164 debate centred on a mid-teens rate [unverified]) and a parallel push from the casinos for compensation or their own skins.

segments.name: Online casino (iGaming) & political direction of travel
segments.headline: No legal iGaming; tribal-exclusive LD 1164 is the only live pathway and its fate turns on the 3 Nov 2026 gubernatorial election.
narrative: Maine has no authorised online casino, no online lottery sales reported here (n/a) and no commercial online poker; the regulated digital channel is mobile sports wagering, which AGA puts at >99% of 2025 sports AGR and we estimate at ~27% of 9M 2026 total GGR. Casino GGR has grown 2-3% a year, so the only material step-change available to the market is iGaming legalisation.

The vehicle is LD 1164, 'An Act to Authorize the Wabanaki Nations to Conduct Internet Gaming', which would extend the tribes' mobile sports exclusivity into online casino. It passed both chambers in 2025 on narrow margins amid gubernatorial opposition and was carried over rather than enacted; its disposition in the 2026 session could not be verified in this research and is marked [unverified]. The commercial casinos (PENN, Churchill Downs) oppose a tribal-exclusive model, citing cannibalisation of a 42%-taxed land-based base; trade coverage in March 2026 already framed the two properties as facing 'competition from new online' products, which we read as a signal that the debate remained live.

The political calendar is decisive. Governor Mills, who signalled a veto, is term-limited; Maine elects a new governor on 3 November 2026 and the 133rd Legislature convenes in January 2027. A sponsor-friendly administration could see a tribal iGaming statute in 2027 with launch in 2028; a sceptical one leaves Maine a two-casino, sports-only state through the forecast horizon. Either way, expect the tax design to borrow from the sports template (10% of AGR) under pressure from the Appropriations Committee to move toward the casino rate.

For B2Tech the strategic position is clear: there is no direct licence to apply for, so optionality must be built through relationships with the four Wabanaki Nations (two of whom — the Houlton Band of Maliseet Indians and the Mi'kmaq Nation — are bundled into the DraftKings sports deal and would be natural candidates for a differentiated iGaming partner), and through a content/platform supplier licence that would be required under any statute. Scale expectations should be modest: a Maine iGaming market would plausibly be in the $150-250m GGR range at maturity (our estimate, benchmarked to New England per-capita comparators), not a top-tier US state.

segments.name: Payments, responsible gambling & advertising
segments.headline: Conventional US rails; 21+ across casino and sports; strict GCU advertising code and a ring-fenced addiction fund — compliance cost is modest but conduct expectations are high.
narrative: Payments are mainstream US: casino floors run on cash and ticket-in/ticket-out (9M funds-in of $393m at Hollywood and $706m at Oxford), while the DraftKings and Caesars apps accept ACH/online banking, debit cards and wallets through their national stacks. The sports wagering framework restricts the use of credit cards to fund accounts [not re-verified today], aligning Maine with the more conservative US states; there is no mobile-money dimension and no payment-blocking regime against offshore operators beyond federal UIGEA mechanics.

Responsible gambling is funded by statute. The Gambling Addiction Prevention and Treatment Fund receives 1% of sports AGR (~$0.49m in 9M 2026) and a share of the 3% GCU administration/gambling addiction earmark on casino slots ($1.68m Hollywood and $2.18m Oxford in 9M 2026); the GCU administers a statewide voluntary self-exclusion programme spanning casinos and sportsbooks, and the minimum age is 21 for casino and sports wagering (18 for lottery and pari-mutuel) [age thresholds not re-verified today]. Helpline signposting (211 Maine / 1-800-GAMBLER) is mandatory in advertising.

Advertising rules under the GCU's sports wagering chapter are among the tighter US codes: no advertising on or directed at college campuses or college-aged audiences, no depiction of under-21s, restrictions on 'free' or 'risk-free' promotional language, mandatory responsible-gambling messaging, and operator liability for affiliate conduct [rule text not re-verified today]. The regime has drawn little enforcement controversy to date, but the January 2025 denial of a permanent licence to the Portland Oddfellas operator shows the Gambling Control Board will exercise discretion on suitability.

For an entrant, the compliance burden is light in money terms but reputationally sensitive: Maine's legislature is attentive to tribal equity and problem-gambling optics, and any iGaming debate will carry stricter advertising and affordability expectations than the sports statute. Operators should expect deposit-limit, time-limit and cooling-off tooling to be table stakes in any future online casino rule set.

highlights.text: Sports hold normalisation is lifting AGR far faster than handle: September AGR +36.5% on handle -3.4%, hold 10.4% vs ~7.4%; 9M handle +10% to $450.2m. A 10% AGR tax with no promo deduction leaves ~90% of AGR with the licensee and its platform partner — the best fiscal terms in the market.

Casino volumes are healthy even if GGR is not: slot funds-in +15.4% at Hollywood and +8.4% at Oxford, with Q3 GGR +4.8% and September +7.5%. The floor is ~1,570 machines, well below the 3,000 statewide cap, so supplier upside exists without any licensing event.
Oxford has started reporting ETG win (from June 2026) in response to an 18% table decline — a live procurement window for electronic table game and cabinet suppliers at the state's larger property.

Tribal iGaming (LD 1164) is the only legal online casino pathway in New England's least-penetrated state; two of the four Wabanaki Nations' rights are bundled into a sports-only DraftKings deal, creating a natural opening for a differentiated iGaming platform partner if the statute passes.

Fiscal dependence creates allies: 9M 2026 casino take of $54.5m funds K-12 education ($19.1m from Oxford alone), harness racing, agricultural fairs and tribal payments — a broad beneficiary coalition that tends to support revenue-raising expansion in Augusta.

Regulatory transparency is high: weekly-updated GCU revenue files by property and product, with distributions itemised to the cent, make diligence and partner monitoring cheap relative to most African jurisdictions B2Tech covers.

lowlights.text: No direct licence route: casinos are a closed duopoly (PENN, Churchill Downs) with statutory supply caps and a 100-mile siting rule; mobile sports is tribal-exclusive with all four nations already contracted (DraftKings ~83%, Caesars). Entry is B2B or via a tribe only.

Casino tax burden of ~42% of GGR (46% on Oxford slots; 1% of coin-in plus 39% at Bangor) compresses operator margins and promotional capacity; any iGaming regime negotiated against this benchmark risks a rate well above the 10% sports template.
Table games are in structural decline: statewide -10.1% in 9M and -10.8% in Q3, with hold down ~250-350bp at both properties and Oxford drop -8.1%; the growth in the land-based market is slots-only.

Scale is small and growth is low: casino GGR is on track for ~$170m in FY2026 (+2-3%) and total market ~$240-245m; even a successful iGaming launch would likely make Maine a sub-$250m online state at maturity (estimate).

Political uncertainty is acute: the LD 1164 outcome could not be verified, the incumbent governor opposed tribal iGaming, and the 3 Nov 2026 election plus a new Legislature in Jan 2027 reset the agenda; sports tax-rate increases (a 16% figure circulated in 2025) remain a live fiscal temptation.

Licensing discretion has teeth: the Gambling Control Board denied a permanent licence to the Portland Oddfellas sportsbook operator in Jan 2025, pausing retail betting; the basis on which First Tracks Investments (Oddfellahs) continues to report in 2026 is unverified — a reminder that suitability findings can abruptly end a retail footprint.

Data gap: sports wagering figures here rely on three corroborating trade reads of the GCU September files rather than the parsed primary PDFs; the Covers tracker shows a ~$6m lower 9M handle. Treat sports AGR and hold as estimates until reconciled.

forecast.intro: Maine does not issue guidance, so the bridge below moves from AGA's FY2025 total of $234.6m (casino $166.4m + sports $68.2m) to our FY2026 estimate. Casinos: 9M GGR $129.4m plus Q4 at +3% on the Q4-25 base of $39.9m gives ~$170.5m (+2.5%), driven by Hollywood slots and Oxford's Q3 recovery, partly offset by continued table erosion. Sports: 9M AGR ~$48.6m plus a Q4 of $22-26m (NFL/NBA peak at ~10% hold on handle growing mid-single digits) gives $70-75m (+3-10%), the whole uplift coming from hold rather than volume. Combined FY2026E ~$241-246m (+3-5%), with state gaming tax of ~$78-80m (casino ~$71.5m at 42%, sports ~$7-7.5m). No iGaming revenue is included in 2026-27; it is the binary swing factor.
forecast.view: Our independent view: **land-based GGR grows 2-3% a year through 2027 with mix shifting further to slots** (tables already 13% of GGR, trending to ~11%), and **sports AGR grows faster than handle as hold settles at 9.5-10.5%** versus 2025's ~7-8% months; **state take rises in line, ~$78-80m in FY2026E**. On rules: the **sports tax rate is more likely to rise than fall** over two years (fiscal pressure plus the 42% casino benchmark make 10% look anomalous to Appropriations), while **iGaming is a coin-flip dependent on the November 2026 governor** — if a supportive administration takes office, expect a tribal-exclusive statute in the 2027 session with launch in 2028 at a mid-teens-to-20% GGR rate and some compensation mechanism for the two casinos; if not, Maine stays sports-only. **Leverage/market structure direction: more concentrated, not less** — DraftKings' ~83% share is unlikely to be challenged without a third skin or iGaming cross-sell. For B2Tech the actionable path is supplier licensing and a tribal relationship now, so that optionality exists when the statute moves.

Any bill to lift the sports wagering tax above 10% of AGR (a 16% figure circulated in 2025) or to change the AGR definition (promo deductibility).

Oxford table/ETG trajectory: table GGR -18% in 9M; watch ETG win ramp (first reported June 2026) and any cabinet/system procurement.
Hollywood Bangor slot momentum (funds-in +15%) and whether PENN seeks a retail book or legislative mobile access.

Full-year 2026 GCU files (early Jan 2027) and any audit restatements — current files are explicitly 'subject to audit'.
